correctness.rationale: For a triangular matrix with \(k\) zero diagonal entries, group invertibility is equivalent to semisimplicity of the zero primary component, hence to rank \(n-k\). The fixed-diagonal count follows from two exhaustive last-coordinate recurrences: a nonzero last diagonal allows every \(q^{n-1}\) final column, while a zero last diagonal requires the final column to lie in an image space of dimension \(n-k\). Both recurrences give \(q^{\binom n2-\binom k2}\). Choosing the nonzero diagonal positions and values yields the stated rank enumerator. A standalone exhaustive verifier agrees for \(q\in\{2,3,5\}\) and for \(\mathbb F_4\), but those finite checks are not used as the all-dimension proof.

value.rationale: Group inversion is a standard generalized-inverse notion, and prior triangular literature is structural rather than enumerative. The new pattern-independence lemma is a natural exact invariant for the full finite triangular algebra, valid in all dimensions and finite fields; it refines the total census by rank and fixed diagonal rather than providing an arbitrary small computation.
